summary: First keep only the letters (lowercased), then check every neighbouring pair: a vowel must be followed by a consonant and vice versa (T3 — string classification + T5 — neighbour comparison). One bad pair is enough to say "Not Alternating".

blocks.title: Read the text and name the vowels
blocks.text: A plain `input()` keeps spaces and symbols — we filter them next. `VOWELS` is a string, so `ch in VOWELS` asks "is this a vowel?".

blocks.title: Keep only the letters, in lowercase
blocks.text: `ch.isalpha()` drops digits, spaces and symbols, so the pattern continues across them (`h3ll0` → `h l l`). `.lower()` matters because `'A' in 'aeiou'` is False.

blocks.title: Assume it alternates
blocks.text: `ok` starts True; the loop below only has to find ONE counter-example to make it False.

blocks.title: Classify each neighbouring pair
blocks.text: `i` starts at 1 so `letters[i - 1]` always exists. For each pair we turn both letters into True/False: "is it a vowel?". With 0 or 1 letters the loop never runs, so the answer is Alternating.

blocks.title: Same type twice in a row → fail
blocks.text: If both are vowels or both are consonants, the two booleans are equal. We set `ok = False` and `break` — no need to check the rest.

blocks.title: Print the result
blocks.text: Exact strings: `Result: Alternating` or `Result: Not Alternating`.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 1000 characters — instant.
pitfalls: Forgetting `.lower()` → uppercase vowels count as consonants.
Checking word by word — the pattern runs across spaces.
